content_html:
Cusco, the ancient capital of the Inca Empire, not only dazzles with its Andean architecture and landscapes, but also with its vibrant festive calendar. Every year, this Peruvian city becomes the scene of some of the most impressive festivities in South America, where Inca heritage, Andean spirituality and Catholic culture are mixed.

Inti Raymi: The Festival of the Sun

The most emblematic celebration of Cusco is, without a doubt, the Inti Raymi. This festival is celebrated every June 24 and represents a tribute to Sun God (Inti). Thousands of people gather at the Sacsayhuamán fortress to relive an ancestral ceremony that recreates Inca rituals with dances, typical costumes and Andean music.

Corpus Christi: Faith and cultural syncretism

A few weeks before Inti Raymi, the Corpus Christi takes center stage historic center of Cusco. It is a massive procession of saints and virgins carried on enormous litters, accompanied by bands and faithful. This celebration reflects the syncretism between Catholicism and the Andean worldview.

Cusco Festival: All June is a celebration

During the month of June, the city lives its «Jubilee Month», with parades, typical dance competitions and concerts. This is an excellent time to learn about the cultural diversity of Cusco and enjoy its gastronomy, crafts and hospitality.

Why visit Cusco during its festivities?

Traveling to Cusco in June allows you to experience a unique connection with the history, spirituality and art of the Andean people. If you are looking for a authentic cultural experience in Peru, these celebrations are an unmissable opportunity.
